# `silk/platform/native/diagnostics`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

The observer of native and wasm programs that reports unhandled errors and traps, with their call
path.

## When to use
`silk.platform.native.start` and `silk.platform.wasi.start` use it around the application. Use it
in a custom runtime: make an observer with [`NativeDiagnostics.make`](#NativeDiagnostics.impl.make), then wrap the application
with [`NativeDiagnostics.observe`](#NativeDiagnostics.impl.observe).

## Details
While the body runs, the observer records the call path and the causes of errors in a pool of
context nodes. When an error is handled, its nodes go back to the pool. When an error is not
handled, the observer writes it with a `NativeReport`. If the pool is empty, the report still
has the error name and its origin, but frames and causes can be missing.

## Gotchas
- The observer does not close the descriptor of the report, and does not end the process.
- An unhandled error gives status 1, also when the report cannot be written.
- A trap writes a report, then the program stops. In an unoptimized native build the report
  also names the functions that called the trapping one, without those of the standard library.
  A wasm program cannot walk its own stack, so the runtime's own trace lists the callers:
  Wasmtime's on WASI, the engine's `Error.stack` on `wasm32-unknown-unknown`.

Import as `NativeDiagnostics` with `import silk.platform.native.diagnostics { NativeDiagnostics }`.

Public declarations: 1.

## `NativeDiagnostics`

```silk
pub struct NativeDiagnostics
```

The observer of native and WASI programs that reports unhandled errors and traps, with their
call path. It has a report writer and a pool of context nodes.

### When to use
`silk.platform.native.start` and `silk.platform.wasi.start` use it around the application. Use
it in a custom runtime: make an observer with [`NativeDiagnostics.make`](#NativeDiagnostics.impl.make), then wrap the
application with [`NativeDiagnostics.observe`](#NativeDiagnostics.impl.observe).

### Details
While the body runs, the observer records the call path and the causes of errors in the pool.
When an error is handled, its nodes go back to the pool. When an error is not handled, the
observer writes it with a `NativeReport`. If the pool is empty, the report still has the
error name and its origin, but frames and causes can be missing.

The report leaves out caller frames from the standard library (module paths that start with
`silk/`), such as the runtime's own `Effect.flatMap`. The origin line is always written, also
when the error was created in the standard library.

Each report starts with the full limits of the `NativeReport`, so one observer can write
several reports. A handler that reports a handled error in its own words, such as the test
runner for a failed expectation, calls `Intrinsic.observeHandled` after it: the observer then
writes only the caller frames of that error.

### Gotchas
- The observer does not close the descriptor of the report, and does not end the process.
- An unhandled error gives status 1, also when the report cannot be written.
- A trap writes a report, then the program stops. In an unoptimized native build the report
  also names the functions that called the trapping one, without those of the standard
  library. A WASI program cannot walk its own stack, so the WASI runtime's own trace lists the
  callers.

## Implementation `NativeDiagnostics`

```silk
impl NativeDiagnostics
```

<a id="NativeDiagnostics.impl.make"></a>

### Associated function `make`

```silk
pub effect fn make(report: NativeReport, capacity: usize) -> NativeDiagnostics
```

Returns an observer that writes with `report`, and has a pool of `capacity` context nodes.

#### Details
It writes nothing. With a capacity of 0, it allocates no pool. If the allocation fails, the
observer works without a pool.

<a id="NativeDiagnostics.impl.observe"></a>

### Method `observe`

```silk
pub fn observe<'env, A, ?R>(self: Self, body: once Effect<'env; A ? R>) -> once Effect<'env; A ? R>
```

Returns an effect that runs `body` under this observer.

#### Details
It does not run `body` now. The observer is released when the effect completes, is
cancelled, or is dropped before it runs. A suspended effect keeps it. The value and the
requirements of `body` are unchanged. `body` must handle its own errors.

#### Gotchas
In the handler of an unhandled error, drop the error value before you call
`Intrinsic.observeUnhandled`. That call returns 1, also when the report cannot be written.
